newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Taurus head sees Michelin ownership as promising.
newsitem.headline: Taurus head sees Michelin ownership as promising.

text.p: The head of Hungarian tyremaker Taurus sees promising prospects after an announcement on Thursday that the Swiss holding company of French tyremaker Michelin had purchased the company.
"I expect developments and I am hopeful," Laszlo Toth, general director of Taurus Rt, told Reuters.
The Swiss-based Compagnie Financiere Michelin was announced as the winner of the tender for a 90 percent stake in Taurus worth 1.6 billion forints and its liabilities of 8.26 billion.

The head of Hungary's privatisation agency, Istvan Kocsis, said Michelin would pay a cash price higher than the nominal value of the two amounts. He also said Michelin agreed to undertake an investment programme of roughly the same value as the purchase price.
"Taurus expects the new owners to bring technological knowledge that only they, as the world's biggest tyremaker, can provide," Toth said.

He declined to elaborate on what Kocsis said would be product range diversification to be implemented by Michelin and added that he did not think the new ownership would be a major boosting factor of Taurus's already high exports.
"We do not need help in that respect," he said. "What Michelin can do is improve productivity, by means which are not necessarily too expensive, but could only be done by them."

Taurus Rt, formerly known as one of Hungary's "dirty dozen" state-owned, loss-making companies, came out of the red in 1994, with a modest 101 million forints pre-tax profit. That rose to 552 million in 1995 and Toth said it would reach some 900 million this year.
He expects sales to grow to about 24 billion forints in 1996 from 18.5 billion last year, maintaining the over 60 percent export proportion.
